pages.title: SCP-02 Scope 2 Inventory Protocol — Rev 4
pages.body:
SCP-02 Scope 2 Inventory Protocol — Revision 4

Controlled copy. Owner: Group Sustainability Reporting. Approved by the Sustainability Steering Committee on 2026-06-18. In force from 2026-07-01 for every Scope 2 inventory struck on or after that date (FY2026 onwards). Supersedes Revision 3 (2025-03-04). Word or PDF copies outside this space are uncontrolled; the April 2026 consultation draft is withdrawn.

1 Scope

1.1 The inventory covers purchased electricity, purchased district steam and purchased chilled water of Talvik Precision Components Inc. and the subsidiaries in Schedule C, under operational control, for the 22 sites of the site register.

1.2 The fiscal year runs 1 October to 30 September. FY2026 is 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

1.3 Every site reports a location-based and a market-based figure in t CO2e.

2 Records of the inventory and the strike date

2.1 The inventory board (monday.com, one item per site) and the summary page in this space are the records of the inventory.

2.2 The inventory is struck when the summary page is published. Activity data, certificate status and factors are taken as the records of reference stand at that moment; a change that reaches a record of reference before the strike is part of the inventory.

3 Emission factors

3.1 Factors come from the Talvik Emission Factor Set (EFS) edition and revision that Schedule A names for the inventory year. A revision includes every erratum issued for it; errata are published as child pages of the EFS page in this space and are not merged into the distributed CSV, so the CSV of an edition is read together with its errata.

3.2 An edition published during or after the fiscal year does not apply to that year unless Schedule A says so.

3.3 The location factor is the EFS "location" row of the site's EFS region (site register); the residual mix is the "residual_mix" row of the same region.

4 Activity data — purchased electricity

4.1 The source of record is the supplier invoice, as filed by Facilities in the Box folder "Facilities — Utility invoices FY2026" (the invoice ledger and any reissued invoice filed beside it). Exports of the ledger kept elsewhere are working copies.

4.2 Where an invoice and a site meter disagree, the invoice governs. The desk raises the discrepancy with the supplier; the invoice stands as billed until the supplier reissues it.

4.3 Exception for estimated invoices: an invoice month with read type E is replaced by the metered consumption of the same period from the energy platform, i.e. the difference between the main meter's month-end register readings that bound the billing period.

4.4 A reissued invoice replaces the invoice it corrects for the whole of its billing period from the moment it is filed in the invoice folder.

4.5 Quantities are taken in the unit the supplier bills; the ledger data dictionary records the accounts not billed in kWh. Convert to MWh before applying factors.

5 Activity data — thermal carriers

5.1 Steam quantities are the pounds (lb) on the supplier's monthly statement lines; chilled water quantities are the ton-hours on the supplier's monthly statement lines.

5.2 Steam energy: MMBtu = lb × enthalpy (Btu/lb) ÷ 1,000,000.

5.3 Enthalpy: where the site returns condensate to the supplier and the supplier credits it (site register "condensate_return" = Yes), use the supplier's net delivered enthalpy; otherwise use the total enthalpy of the delivered steam. Both come from the supplier's enthalpy note for the period.

5.4 Steam factors: the location-based figure uses the EFS district-steam default of the revision in force. The market-based figure uses the supplier's plant-specific factor only where that factor has been verified by an independent third party; an unverified, preliminary or indicative supplier factor is not used and the EFS default applies.

5.5 Chilled water: kWh-equivalent = ton-hours × 12,000 ÷ 3,412.14 ÷ COP, where COP is the plant's measured annual coefficient of performance for the fiscal year as stated in the supplier's annual statement. Design, nameplate or "up to" efficiencies are not a measured COP. Where the statement gives no measured COP, use the Schedule B default.

5.6 Chilled water takes the location factor and the residual mix of the site's EFS region. Contractual instruments are not applied to chilled water.

6 Contractual instruments — quality criteria for the market-based figure

An instrument reduces a site's market-based electricity only if it satisfies every clause below. The registry status is read in the registry account mirror (Airtable), which Greenledger syncs from the registries.

6.1 Instruments apply to purchased electricity only.

6.2 Vintage: the generation period on the certificate lies wholly within 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2026 (six months before the fiscal year to three months after it).

6.3 Market boundary: the certificate is issued in the market where the site consumes. US sites: NRR RECs. Sites in Germany, the Netherlands and Poland: EECS Guarantees of Origin issued through AIB member registries. Sites in Great Britain: Ofgem REGOs only; Guarantees of Origin are not accepted for GB consumption.

6.4 Retirement: the registry shows the certificate as Retired at the strike date. Active, instructed, scheduled, pending or reversed retirements do not qualify.

6.5 Beneficiary: the certificate is retired on behalf of Talvik Precision Components Inc. or one of the subsidiaries in Schedule C. Retirements for any other party, including former group companies, do not qualify.

6.6 No double claim: a certificate claimed in any earlier inventory (a claim period of an earlier fiscal year, or a listing in that year's final inventory) is not claimed again.

6.7 Generator age: the generating facility was commissioned on or after 1 January 2011.

6.8 Power purchase agreements count only through the certificates they convey to Talvik, and those certificates must themselves meet 6.2 to 6.7. A contract that settles financially without conveying the attributes to Talvik is not an instrument, whatever volume it names.

6.9 Site and volume: an instrument covers only the site named in its registry retirement record ("Site claimed"), up to that site's purchased electricity for the year. Volume above that is not carried to another site or to another year.

6.10 Every excluded instrument is recorded with the clause it fails.

7 Calculation

7.1 Location-based t CO2e = (electricity MWh + chilled-water MWh-equivalent) × location factor + steam MMBtu × EFS district-steam default ÷ 1,000.

7.2 Market-based t CO2e = (electricity MWh − MWh covered by qualifying instruments) × residual mix + chilled-water MWh-equivalent × residual mix + steam MMBtu × market-based steam factor ÷ 1,000.

7.3 Where the EFS revision in force publishes no residual-mix factor for a region, the location factor of that region is used in its place.

7.4 Carry full precision through the calculation and round each site figure to one decimal place at the end. Totals are the sum of the rounded site figures as entered on the board.

8 Reporting

8.1 On the board, each site item carries "Location-based tCO2e" and "Market-based tCO2e" as numbers to one decimal place, and "Instrument applied": the registry Certificate ID of every qualifying instrument for the site, in ascending order, separated by a semicolon and a space; or the words Residual mix where no instrument qualifies.

8.2 The summary page states the two totals and lists every excluded instrument by its registry Certificate ID, or by its contract reference where no certificate was conveyed.

Schedule A — EFS edition and revision by inventory year

Inventory yearEFS editionRevision in forceNote

FY2025EFS-20242024.1
FY2026EFS-20252025.2 (Erratum 2 of 2026-02-17)EFS-2026 was published 2026-08-14, after the start of FY2026; it is not used for FY2026.

Schedule B — constants

12,000 Btu per ton-hour; 3,412.14 Btu per kWh; default chilled-water plant COP 4.0; 1 MWh = 1,000 kWh; 1 t = 1,000 kg.

Schedule C — subsidiaries in the organisational boundary (FY2026)

Talvik Precision Components GmbH (DE); Talvik Precision Components B.V. (NL); Talvik Precision Components Sp. z o.o. (PL); Talvik Precision Components Ltd (GB). Talvik Marine Systems LLC was divested on 2025-06-30 and is outside the boundary from FY2026.

Revision history: Rev 3 2025-03-04; Rev 4 2026-06-18 (precedence of invoices, steam enthalpy, measured COP, GB market boundary, site-bound instruments, no residual mix fallback to location factor, Schedule A).

The EFS is Talvik's single source of grid, residual-mix and district-energy factors. Each edition is distributed as a CSV by the data steward; errata for an edition are child pages of this page. Which edition and revision applies to an inventory year is fixed by the Scope 2 protocol, Schedule A.

messages.subject: Energy platform — validated month-end register reads posted (MDV-2026-11)
messages.bodyPreview: Hello desk, the annual register validation MDV-2026-11 is complete. We compared every FY2026 month-end register on the energy platform with the load-profile logs downloaded from the main meters during the November field campaign. Every automatic (AMR) month-end matched its log. Four month-ends that had been loaded by hand or by backfill did not, and the validated register values replaced them on the platform today: M-06-01 Elkhart (TPC-06) 2025-12-31 23:59 — manual read taken on 29 Dec at 16:40 and loaded as the 31 Dec month-end: 6,689,555 kWh replaced by 6,720,875 kWh; M-08-01 Macon (TPC-08) 2026-04-30 23:59 — manual read taken on 28 Apr at 15:30 and loaded as the 30 Apr month-end: 9,785,133 kWh replaced by 9,820,163 kWh; M-10-01 Salem (TPC-10) 2026-02-28 23:59 — manual read of 28 Feb keyed with two digits transposed: 9,857,661 kWh replaced by 9,875,661 kWh; M-17-01 Eindhoven (TPC-17) 2026-06-30 23:59 — the 9 July backfill loaded the 30 Jun 00:00 interval register instead of the 30 Jun 24:00 register: 15,521,883 kWh replaced by 15,529,763 kWh. The platform readings of these meters now carry the validated values; extracts and exports taken before today (including the 3 October export) still show the old ones. Lena Okafor, Energy platform administrator, Facilities Shared Services
